the filamentous, intracellular aggregate, alcoholic hyaline from human alcoholic liversexhibits lectin-like activity.
we have detected lectin-like activity associated with intermediate filaments.
the intracellular filamentous aggregate, alcoholic hyaline (AH), is capable of binding the glycoprotein, horseradishes peroxidase (HRP).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterization of the intracellular filamentous aggregate, alcoholic hyaline (AH).
the characterization of alcoholic hyaline as a possible marker for the alcoholic fatty liver.
the detection of lectinlike activity in alcoholic hyaline and the possible implications of such activity for the development of alcoholic hepatitis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
alcoholic hyaline is a filamentous aggregate of a protein which has the ability to bind to carbohydrate-containing molecules, such as horseradish-peroxidase.
alcoholic hyaline is a filamentous, carbohydrate-binding glycoprotein, the first such structure to be described in mammalian cells.

the lectin-like activity of alcoholic hyaline is a specific, saturable, thermolabile, pH-sensitive, and carbohydrate-sensitive phenomenon that is highly reproducible and that the binding of the enzyme is not a passive phenomenon but rather is a specific interaction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
alcoholic hyaline contains a lectin that may play a role in the pathogenesis of alcoholic liver disease.
we have shown the presence of a lectin-like substance on the surface of alcoholic hyaline filaments.
the alcoholic hyaline filaments have a lectin-like activity and that this activity may be a general property of all intermediate filaments.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the binding of lectin is not a passive phenomenon, but rather a “active” phenomenon that involves carbohydrate groups in the enzyme and that this lectin may play an important role in intracellular transport.
the lectin-like activity is not restricted to the cytoplasmic face of the alcoholic hyaline filaments, but is present throughout their length.
alcoholic hyaline is not a random aggregate of proteins, but rather is a complex, organized structure with a specific function.
